title: Autoscaler frozen window causes reserved-pool burst shortfall and customer escalations
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden 5-10x latency and token throttles between 2026-03-05T02:10Z and 2026-03-05T03:00Z in the eu-west and us-east regions. Root cause investigation found the dedicated autoscaler entered a multi-minute frozen window during a high-cardinality tenant surge, preventing proactive scale-ups and causing reserved pools to exhaust burst credits. Several tenants (notably NimbusHealth and LumenDocs) hit their burst limits and observed request failures and degraded SLA. This ticket drives the bugfix, emergency mitigations, customer comms, and follow-up hardening work.
reproduction_steps: Replay traffic trace from 2026-03-05 (s3://redwood-logs/trace-2026-03-05-euw-us.json) into a staging autoscaler cluster
Simulate 2.5x tenant fanout with synthetic warmup disabled to replicate cold-start pressure
Observe autoscaler leadership transitioning and frozen decision window when the leader's horizon estimator receives a null sensor sample
Confirm reserved-pool headroom drops below safety threshold and burst-credit accounting stops updating
root_cause_summary: An edge-case race between autoscaler leadership handoff and the sensor aggregation loop allowed a zero-sample to propagate into the horizon estimator. The estimator interpreted the sample as 'no-load' and suppressed scale-up signals for the configured frozen_window (default 120s). Combined with a separate burst-accounting ledger checkpoint bug that skipped updates during leader re-election, the system failed to allocate headroom and exhausted burst credits for small-to-medium tenants.
